newsitem.title: USA: Intensiva HealthCare sees profit for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Intensiva HealthCare sees profit for 1997.

text.p: Intensiva HealthCare Corp said Wednesday it was increasingly confident that it will post a profit in 1997.

Earlier, Intensiva reported a second quarter profit of $0.02 a share on 10.5 million shares outstanding, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.64 on 1.6 million shares. Sales nearly quadrupled to $3.6 million from $14.3 million.

"This impressive performance increases our confidence that a profit will be earned for 1997, while we absorb the expense of building our network of acute long-term care hospitals," David Cross, president, said in a statement.
In 1996, Intensiva had a loss of $1.48 a share on 3.4 million shares outstanding.
Intensiva provides highly specialized, acute long-term care for critically ill or injured patients who require intensive medical monitoring and treatment.
Cross said Intensiva's operations are cost-effective since it leases under-utilized space in leading hospitals.
In the second quarter, Intensiva opened hospitals in Flint and Mt. Clemens, Mich., and in Topeka, Kan., bringing the total in operation to 13.
